units: <cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 2:7">Ber. II, 7</cite> <he>וכשמת … קבל עליו ת׳</he> when his slave Ṭabi died, he accepted condolence for him.
<cite ref="Ketubot 10b:5">Keth. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>ת׳ של הבל ניחמו וכ׳</he> R. G. offered this man a vain consolation; <cite ref="Bava Batra 16b:9">B. Bath. 16ᵇ</cite>.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 16b:17">Ab. Zar. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>נכנסו … ולא קיבל ת׳</he> (not <he>ק׳ עליו</he>) his disciples came to console him, but he would accept no consolation; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 937:13">Yalk. Prov. 937</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 551:5">Yalk. Mic. 551</cite>.
<cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 30:1">Ab. d’R. N. ch. XXX</cite> <he>תַּנְחוּמֵי אבלים וכ׳</he> comforting the mourners, visiting the sick, and deeds of kindness bring good into the world.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 29:1">Pesik. R. s. 29-30</cite> <he>עמדי וקבלי כוס ת׳</he> stand up and accept the cup of consolation; <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 29:1">ib.</cite> <he>כוס תַּנְחוּמַיִךְ</he>; <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 29:1">ib.</cite> <he>הרי תַּנְחוּמֶיךָ נתונים לך</he> thy consolations are given back to thee (I will not accept them); a. fr.
